tips.intro: Getting Over It on Pixelsprout is a climbing game where an orange cat in a flower pot drags itself up a pile of giant Scratch code blocks with a long hammer. This is a fan-made Scratch remake, not the original game. These tips come from real runs, including the spots where falls kept happening.
tips: Use slow, wide sweeps of the mouse. In one run, a steady circular motion lifted the cat off the opening blocks and onto the top of the tall upright when clicked block at 0'16 on the timer.
Hook the hammer head over the top edge of a block before you pull. The pot only moves when the hammer head is pressing against something, so find an edge first.
Ease off the mouse when the pot lands somewhere flat. The cat keeps some momentum after you stop, so give it a moment to settle before the next move.
The tall upright block right after the start is the first real wall. Plant the hammer high on its face and pull down in short strokes instead of one big swing.
Past the tall block, a green block with a plus sign and a long purple play sound Meow until done block form the next ledges. Aim for their flat top surfaces.
The blue water at the bottom is where falls end. In an earlier session, a drop into it sent the cat back near the start and the timer went back close to zero.
Watch the timer in the top right corner. It runs the whole time, so it is a fair way to measure whether a new approach is actually faster.
After a fall, climb the first few low blocks slowly as a warm-up before the tall block, rather than rushing straight back to where you fell.
tips.conclusion: Treat each block as its own small puzzle. Hook an edge, pull a short distance, settle, then plan the next move.

extra_sections.heading: Getting onto the tall when clicked block
paragraphs: This block stands on its end right after the low opening pile, and it is the first climb that needs more than a short push. Bring the cat up against its base, then reach the hammer head as high up the face as it will go.

Pull down in short strokes to lift the pot. Once the pot is level with the top, sweep the hammer over the far side and drag the cat across. In testing, the cat was sitting on top of this block 16 seconds into the run.

extra_sections.heading: The green plus block and the purple Meow block
paragraphs: Beyond the tall block, the path continues over a green operator block with a plus sign and then a long purple play sound Meow until done block that slopes upward. A yellow note box reading Getting Over it, Scratch Edition, Remix by Raph112star hangs above this area.

The purple block is long and tilted, so keep the hammer planted on its top surface and move along it a little at a time. By 0'38 on the timer the cat had reached it, with the note box hanging just above.

controls.intro: The whole game is played with the mouse. The hammer head follows your cursor around the cat, and every move you make comes from where you plant it and which way you pull.
controls.desktop: Move the mouse to swing the hammer around the cat. Press the hammer head against a block and pull the cursor the opposite way to push the pot up or along. No clicking is needed once a run starts. In an earlier session, arrow keys and WASD did nothing.
controls.mobile: A Mobile Controls toggle sits in the lower right corner of the play area, and it showed Disabled while playing with a mouse. Touch controls were not tested, so how they feel on a touch screen is unconfirmed.
tips: On the start screen, choose New Game to begin. Sound Effects and Commentary can be switched from the same menu.
Small, steady mouse movements give the most control. Fast flicks tend to tip the pot over.
The timer in the top right starts when the run starts, so you can watch the menu for as long as you like first.
Use the full screen button in the top right corner for more room to move the mouse.

beginner-guide.intro: New to this version of Getting Over It? Here is what is on screen, what you are trying to do and how the first minute of a run usually goes.
beginner-guide.what_it_is: Getting Over It is a slow, physics-based climbing game. You control the Scratch cat, sitting in a brown flower pot, through a long hammer that follows your mouse. This Pixelsprout version is a Scratch remix: its start screen reads Scratch Edition Remix by Raph112star, and everything you climb is made of oversized Scratch code blocks, such as yellow when clicked blocks with green flags, a green plus operator and a purple play sound Meow block. The goal is to climb as high as you can, with blue water waiting below the blocks.
first_steps: Wait for the game to load, accept the notice if one appears, then press New Game.
Before you climb, move the mouse in a slow circle and watch how the hammer swings around the pot.
Hook the hammer head on the nearest yellow block and pull back to drag the cat onto it.
Cross the low opening pile until you reach the tall upright when clicked block.
Climb the tall block in short pulls, then look for the green plus block on the other side.
If you fall into the water, start the low blocks again slowly instead of rushing.
beginner-guide.who_its_for: Players who enjoy a stubborn precision challenge and can laugh off losing progress, and anyone who knows Scratch and wants to see its code blocks used as climbing terrain.

extra_sections.heading: What the start screen shows
paragraphs: The menu shows the title, the line Scratch Edition Remix by Raph112star, a New Game option and toggles for Sound Effects and Commentary. A High Score label reading TOP 25 sits in the top left, and a World Record time appears in the top right.
Once you press New Game, the menu goes away and a run timer takes the place of the record time in the corner.

similar.intro: Getting Over It is about one awkward control scheme and a lot of patience. Every move happens through a hammer, progress is slow and a single slip can throw away a minute of climbing. If you liked that mix of physics, careful mouse control and starting over without much fuss, try more games from the Pixelsprout catalog next. When you pick one, look for games where the challenge comes from controlling your own movement rather than from enemies or timers.

faqs.question: Is this the original Getting Over It?
faqs.answer: No. The start screen credits it as a Scratch Edition Remix by Raph112star, and the levels are built from giant Scratch code blocks.

faqs.question: How do you move in Getting Over It?
faqs.answer: You only control the hammer. Move the mouse so the hammer head presses against a block, then pull the cursor the other way to push the cat and its pot.

faqs.question: Do the arrow keys or WASD do anything?
faqs.answer: No. Arrow keys and WASD had no effect when they were tried in an earlier session. The game is played with the mouse alone.

faqs.question: What happens if you fall into the water?
faqs.answer: The blue water at the bottom ends the climb. In an earlier session, a fall into it sent the cat back near the start and the timer reset close to zero.

faqs.question: What is the first hard part?
faqs.answer: The tall upright when clicked block right after the starting pile. Plant the hammer high on its face and pull in short strokes to get over the top.

faqs.question: Can you turn off the commentary?
faqs.answer: Yes. The start screen has separate Sound Effects and Commentary toggles next to the New Game option.

faqs.question: What do the timer and World Record show?
faqs.answer: A timer in the top right corner counts up during a run. The start screen shows a World Record time in the same spot and a High Score TOP 25 label in the top left.
